pages.text: Day 33. Every machine is built around a processor one tier below its own. There are seven tiers:$(br)$(li)I Photonic$(li)II Qubit$(li)III Topological$(li)IV Hyperdimensional$(li)V Cosmic$(li)VI Ontological$(li)VII Transfinite

A processor needs a $(thing)board$(), $(thing)dies$() of its tier, the previous tier's processor and femto- or attoscale $(thing)components$(), joined with $(fluid)solder$(). From tier IV on, only the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() can assemble them.

The early tiers follow real research: logic carried by light instead of electrons, then $(thing)qubits$() that hold superpositions, then $(thing)topological$() qubits whose information is braided into a shape that noise cannot easily undo. Past tier III, I am naming things as I go.
Tier I processor. Computes with light.$(br2)Made in $(item)Metamaterial Weaver$().
A fault-tolerant array of logical qubits.$(br2)Made in $(item)Matrioshka Brain$().
Tier III processor. Fault-tolerant by geometry.$(br2)Made in $(item)Femto Fabricator$().
Tier IV processor. Its logic gates take inputs from directions that do not exist.$(br2)Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().
